HON'BLE MR JUSTICE H.T. NARENDRA PRASAD  ORAL JUDGMENT This appeal under Section 173(1) of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (hereinafter referred to as 'the Act')
has been filed by the Corporation being aggrieved by the judgment dated 02.02.2018 passed by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Bengaluru (SCCH.13) (hereinafter referred to as 'the Tribunal') in MVC No.5719/2016.

2. Facts giving rise to the filing of the appeal briefly stated are that on 25.03.2016 at about 8.05 p.m., when the claimant was proceeding as a pillion rider on motorcycle bearing registration No.KA-03/HJ-3335 on Airport main road, near Suranjandas road signal, Bengaluru, at that time, a BMTC bus bearing registration No.KA-01/FA-2172 being driven by its driver at a high speed and in a rash and negligent manner, dashed to the vehicle of the claimant.
As a result of the aforesaid accident, the claimant sustained grievous injuries and was hospitalized.
The claimant filed a petition under Section 166 of the Act, seeking compensation.
It was pleaded that she spent significant amount towards medical expenses, conveyance charges and other related costs.
It was further pleaded that the accident occurred solely on account of rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle by its driver.
4. Upon service of notice, the respondent appeared through counsel and filed written statement denying the averments made in the claim petition.

5. On the basis of the pleadings of the parties, the Claims Tribunal framed the issues and thereafter,
recorded the evidence.
The claimant, in order to prove the case, examined herself as PW-1, and Dr.S.Ramachandra was examined as PW-2, and got exhibited documents namely Ex.P1 to Ex.P19.
On behalf of the respondents, one witness was examined as RW-1 and no documents were got exhibited.
The Claims Tribunal, by the impugned judgment, inter alia
, held that the accident took place on NC: 2024:KHC:37508 account of rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle by its driver, as a result of which, the claimant sustained injuries.

The Tribunal further held that the claimant is entitled to a compensation of Rs.3,99,536/- along with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. and directed the Corporation to deposit the compensation amount along with interest.

Being aggrieved,
the present appeal has been filed.

sentences.text:
The learned counsel for the Corporation raised the following contentions:
(i) Firstly, the accident occurred due to the negligence of the rider of the motorcycle.
When the driver of the bus was taking 'U' turn, the rider of the motorcycle came at a high speed, in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the bus.
(ii) Secondly, IMV report is very clear that the entire front portion of the motorcycle was damaged and therefore, the rider of the motorcycle was negligent in causing the accident.
But, the Tribunal, contrary to the NC: 2024:KHC:37508 materials available on record has wrongly held that the driver of the bus is negligent in causing the accident.
(iii) Thirdly, considering the injuries suffered by the claimant and the medical records, the overall compensation awarded by the Tribunal is on the higher side.

Hence, he sought to allow the appeal.
7.

On the other hand, learned counsel for the claimant raised the following contentions:
(i) Firstly, the accident occurred due to the negligence of the driver of the bus.
In the junction, the driver suddenly took 'U' turn and dashed against the motorcycle.
Therefore, the Tribunal rightly held that the driver of the bus was negligent in causing the accident.
(ii) Secondly, considering the evidence of the doctor and medical records, the overall compensation awarded by the Tribunal is on the lower side.
Hence, he sought to dismiss the appeal.
Heard the learned counsel for the parties and perused the judgment and award of the Tribunal and the original records.

9. The case of the claimant is that, on 25.03.2016 at about 8.05 p.m., when the claimant was proceeding as a pillion rider on motorcycle bearing registration No.KA- 03/HJ-3335 on Airport main road, near Suranjandas road signal, Bengaluru, at that time, a BMTC bus bearing registration No.KA-01/FA-2172 being driven by its driver at a high speed and in a rash and negligent manner,
dashed to the vehicle of the claimant.
As a result of the aforesaid accident, the claimant sustained grievous injuries and was hospitalized.
After recovering from the injuries she filed the claim petition.
To prove her case, she has been examined as PW1 and produced 19 documents.

10. Under the Motor Vehicles Act in the claim petition before the Claims Tribunal the standard of proof is much below than what is required in a criminal case as NC: 2024:KHC:37508 well as in the civil case.

No doubt, before the Tribunal, there must be some material on the basis of which the Tribunal can arrive or decide things necessary to decide for awarding compensation, but the Tribunal is not expected to take or to adopt a nicety of a civil or criminal case.

After all it is a The Managing Director vs Smt Vani Athani on 12 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/46566838/
3 summary enquiry and it is the legislation for the welfare of the Society.

sentences.text: The proceedings under the Motor Vehicles Act are not akin to the proceedings under civil rules.
Hence, strict rules of evidence are not required to be followed in this regard.

In the case of MANGLA RAM -v- ORIENTAL INSURANCE COMPANY LIMITED (2018) 5 SCC 656, the Hon'ble Apex Court has held as hereinbelow:
"25.

entities.text: MANGLA RAM -v- ORIENTAL INSURANCE COMPANY LIMITED (2018) 5 SCC 656
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In Dulcina Fernandes, this Court examined similar situation where the evidence of claimant's eyewitness was discarded by the Tribunal and that the respondent in that case was acquitted in the criminal case concerning the accident.

This Court,
however, opined that it cannot be overlooked that upon investigation of the case registered against the respondent, prima facie, materials showing negligence were found to put him on trial.

The Court restated the NC: 2024:KHC:37508 settled principle that the evidence of the claimants ought to be examined by the Tribunal on the touchstone of preponderance of probability and certainly the standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt could not have been applied."
11.
In her evidence, PW1 has reiterated the statement made in the claim petition.
She has specifically stated that the driver of the bus was negligent in causing the accident.
Immediately after he accident, a complaint has been lodged on the next day, against the driver of the bus.
Police have registered FIR as per Ex.,P1.
After thorough investigation they have filed charge sheet against the driver of the bus.
The police have also drawn a sketch as per Ex.P3.
It is very clear from the sketch that the driver of the bus was moving from west to east and the motorcycle was moving from east to west.
In the junction, the driver of the bus suddenly took 'U' turn and entered into the other side of the road and dashed against the motorcycle.
Therefore, it is very clear from the sketch, mahazar and IMV report that the driver of the bus NC: 2024:KHC:37508 was negligent in causing the accident.
The Tribunal has rightly held that the driver of the bus is negligent in causing the accident.

Re.quantum:
12. Considering the injuries suffered by the claimant and the medical records, the overall compensation awarded by the Tribunal is just and reasonable.

13. In the result, the following order is passed:
(i) The appeal is dismissed.
(ii) The judgment and award passed by the Tribunal is confirmed.
(iii) The amount in deposit is ordered to be transferred to the Tribunal, forthwith.
